title: App Compaction、CachedAppOptimizer、onTrimMemory 与缓存释放
key_conclusions: App-side trim and system-side app compaction are pre-kill pressure reduction opportunities.
App Compaction changes resident page state and is not equivalent to Java object collection.
onTrimMemory is useful only when the app releases rebuildable, low-value caches with acceptable restore cost.
Successful mitigation must reduce memory buckets, PSI, lmkd kills, and preserve recovery experience.
shallow_points: The article does not include real CachedAppOptimizer logs or dumpsys output from a target Android version.
It does not quantify restore latency after cache release or compaction.
It does not validate all trim levels across foreground service, cached, and multi-process apps.
It does not include a runnable low-memory lab that triggers trim, compaction, and lmkd in one scenario.
